scope: Conservatively surface unresolved GCC specs include directives in controlled semantic-adapter build identities without promoting compiler closure.

profile.name: compilerBuiltinSpecs
profile.includeObservation: Counts known file-level %include/%include_noerr and conditional %:include(...) spellings in the captured built-in specs dump and digest-bound main external specs file.

statuses.no-includes-detected: Both inspected sources are bound and no known include spelling was found; this is not a complete effective compiler contract.
statuses.partial: At least one include spelling exists; targets are not resolved or content-bound.
statuses.unavailable: The main external specs identity or source capture is unavailable.

profile.externalSpecsRecheck: Re-read and compare against the previously captured main-specs SHA-256 at each existing controlled-build profile verification.

limitations: The detector recognizes known GCC syntax but is not a specs-language parser and does not resolve include targets.
GCC startfile-prefix/multilib resolution was established by prior research, but no native GNU driver was available for runtime qualification.
This does not close compiler subprocesses, linker-consumed inputs, SDK/sysroot content, or runtime images.
The host's gcc/g++ identify as AppleClang; GNU controls are synthetic only.
nextGate: On a native GNU/Linux runner, observe or resolve actual effective specs includes using GCC's startfile-prefix and multilib semantics, then content-bind every selected target. Keep direct-only pair refusal until all compiler, linker, SDK, runtime, and typed capability gates close.
